<|endoftext|> Lily and Tom were playing in the garden.
They liked to dig holes and look for bugs.
Lily found a big worm and showed it to Tom.
"Look, Tom, a worm!" Lily said.
"Wow, it is long and slimy!" Tom said.
"Can I touch it?" Lily nodded and gave him the worm.
Tom held it in his hand and felt it wriggle.
"Where does it live?" Tom asked.
Lily pointed to the hole.
"It lives in the dirt.
It makes the dirt good for the plants." Tom wanted to see the worm's home.
He put the worm back in the hole and peered inside.
He saw that the hole was deep and dark.
He wondered what else was in there.
"Can we enter the hole?" Tom asked.
Lily shook her head.
"No, Tom, it is too small for us.
And it is dirty.
We will get our shirts dirty." Tom did not listen.
He was curious.
He crawled closer to the hole and stuck his head inside.
He saw more worms and some shiny stones.
He reached for a stone, but then he felt something bite his ear.
"Ow!" Tom cried.
He pulled his head out of the hole and saw a big ant on his ear.
The ant was angry and had big jaws.
"Tom, are you okay?" Lily asked.
She saw the ant and the blood on Tom's ear.
She was scared.
Tom was not okay.
He was hurt and scared.
He dropped the worm and ran to the house.
He wanted his mom to help him.
Lily followed him.
She felt sorry for Tom.
She learned that it was not good to enter the worm's hole.
She decided to play with something else.
<|endoftext|> Lily was very happy.
It was her birthday.
She had a big cake with four candles.
She had many presents from her mom and dad and her friends.
She wanted to open them all.
But her mom said, "Wait, Lily.
You have to close your eyes and make a wish first.
Then you can blow the candles and open your presents." Lily did not want to close her eyes.
She wanted to see her presents.
She said, "No, mom.
I want to open them now.
Please, please, please." Her mom said, "Lily, you have to be patient.
Closing your eyes is part of the fun.
You can wish for anything you want.
Maybe you will get it." Lily thought for a moment.
She wondered what she could wish for.
She looked at her presents.
She saw a big box with a bow.
She wondered what was inside.
She decided to close her eyes and make a wish.
She said, "I wish for a puppy.
A cute and fluffy puppy.
I want to play with it and hug it and name it Spot." She opened her eyes and blew the candles.
Everyone clapped and cheered.
She smiled and thanked her mom and dad and her friends.
She reached for the big box with the bow.
She opened it and gasped.
Inside was a puppy.
A cute and fluffy puppy.
It wagged its tail and licked her face.
She was so happy.
She said, "Wow, mom.
Wow, dad.
You gave me a puppy.
Thank you, thank you, thank you." Her mom and dad hugged her and said, "You're welcome, Lily.
Happy birthday.
We love you." Lily loved them too.
She loved her puppy.
She named it Spot.
She played with it and hugged it and shared her cake with it.
It was the best birthday ever.
<|endoftext|> Lily has a dog named Spot.
Spot is white with black spots.
Lily loves Spot very much, but sometimes Spot is naughty.
Spot likes to run and play in the mud, and he does not like to wash.
One day, Lily and Spot go to the park with Mommy.
Spot sees a big puddle of mud and runs to it.
He jumps and splashes and rolls in the mud.
He gets very dirty and wet.
Lily calls him, but he does not listen.
He thinks it is fun.
Mommy is not happy.
She says, "Spot, you are a naughty dog!
You need to wash.
Come here, now!" But Spot does not come.
He runs away from Mommy and Lily.
He thinks it is a game.
Lily and Mommy chase Spot around the park.
They try to catch him, but he is too fast.
He runs and runs, and makes more mud.
He gets more dirty and wet.
Lily and Mommy get dirty and wet, too.
Finally, they catch Spot.
They take him to a fountain.
They wash him with water and soap.
They wash themselves, too.
Spot does not like it.
He shakes and shivers and whines.
He wants to go back to the mud.
Lily says, "Spot, you are a silly dog.
You need to wash.
You cannot be dirty and wet.
You will get sick.
And you will make the house dirty, too.
You have to be clean and dry.
And you have to listen to Mommy and me.
Do you understand?" Spot looks at Lily with his big brown eyes.
He licks her face.
He says, "Woof, woof." He means, "I'm sorry.
I love you.
I will try to be good." Lily hugs Spot.
She says, "I love you, too, Spot.
You are a good dog.
But please, no more mud.
OK?" Spot nods.
He says, "Woof, woof." He means, "OK.
No more mud.
Promise." Mommy smiles.
She says, "That's a good boy, Spot.
Now let's go home and have a snack.
And maybe a nap.
You must be tired after all that running." Lily and Spot agree.
They are tired and hungry.
They go home with Mommy.
They have a snack and a nap.
They are clean and dry and happy.
They are a good family.
The end.

"Maybe we can.

"Okay, let's ask Mommy.

She says yes to Ben and Lily.

Or she will order pizza from the store.

She is happy to see them playing with shapes.

<|endoftext|> Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play together.

She helped him stand on the scale and looked at the number.

She understood that she was special and had a gift too.
She felt happy and proud of herself.
She looked at Tom and smiled.
He smiled back.
They held hands and sang a song with the other people in the church.
They thanked God for making them twins and for giving them each other.
They felt happy and healthy.
<|endoftext|> Lily and Max were playing in the park.
They liked to go on the slide, the swings and the seesaw.
They had a lot of fun together.
But one day, Lily saw a big slide on the other side of the park.
She wanted to try it, but Max was scared.

She said, "You are a baby.

He wished Lily would come back.
Lily reached the big slide.
She climbed up the ladder and looked down.
She felt a little scared, but she did not want to admit it.
She said to herself, "I can do this.
I am brave." She pushed herself down the slide.
But the slide was not fun.
It was too high and too fast.
It made Lily dizzy and sick.
It also had a bump in the middle that hurt her back.
And the wind was cold and bitter.
It made her shiver and cry.
Lily wished she had stayed with Max.
She wished she had listened to him.
She wished she had been kinder to him.
She realized she had made a mistake.
She got off the slide and ran back to Max.
She said, "I am sorry, Max.
You were right.
The big slide was not fun.
It was scary and painful and cold.
I should have stayed with you.
You are my friend.
Can you forgive me?" Max saw Lily's tears and heard her words.
He felt sorry for her.
He said, "It's okay, Lily.
I forgive you.
You are my friend too.
Come on, let's go on the small slide.
It is safer and nicer.
And we can have fun together." Lily and Max hugged and smiled.
They went on the small slide and had a lot of fun together.
They learned to listen to each other and to be kind to each other.
They were happy.

<|endoftext|> Tom and Mia were at the beach with their mom and dad.
They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water.
They also liked to look for shells and rocks and other things that the sea left behind.
One day, they saw a big crab on the shore.
It had a hard shell and two big claws and lots of legs.
Tom wanted to catch it and put it in his bucket.
He thought it would be a cool pet.
Mia was scared of the crab.
She thought it would pinch her or hurt her.
She wanted to leave it alone.
"Come on, Mia, let's catch the crab!" Tom said.
He ran towards the crab with his bucket and his net.
"No, Tom, don't do it!
The crab is ancient and angry!
It will bite you!" Mia said.
She ran after Tom and tried to stop him.
The crab saw Tom and Mia coming.
It did not like to be bothered.
It raised its claws and snapped them.
It made a loud noise that sounded like "clack, clack, clack!" Tom and Mia stopped in their tracks.
They were both afraid of the crab now.
They turned around and ran back to their mom and dad.
"Mom, dad, there's a big crab over there!
It's ancient and angry and it clacks!" Tom said.
"Really?
Let's go and see it.
Maybe we can learn something about it," mom said.
"No, mom, no!
We don't want to see it!
It's scary!" Mia said.
She insisted that they stay away from the crab.
Mom and dad smiled.
They knew that the crab was not really ancient or angry.
It was just a normal crab that wanted to be left alone.
They decided to respect the crab's wishes and not bother it.
They also decided to teach Tom and Mia more about crabs and other animals that live in the sea.
They hoped that Tom and Mia would learn to appreciate and respect them, and not be afraid of them.
<|endoftext|> Lily was eager to play with her new toy.
It was a big, soft bunny that could jump and make noises.
She got it for her birthday from her grandma.
She loved it so much that she wanted to show it to her friend Mia, who lived next door.
She ran to her closet and grabbed the bunny.
She put it in her backpack and zipped it up.
She ran to the door and put on her shoes.
She was about to go outside when her mom stopped her.
"Where are you going, Lily?" her mom asked.

I have a new toy to show her.

She wanted to play with Mia and her bunny.
She did not want to wait.
She did not like the rain.

The rain is not fair.

Maybe you can call Mia and tell her about your toy.
Or you can read a book or draw a picture.

She wanted to go outside and jump with her bunny and Mia.
She did not want to listen to her mom.

She ran to her room and slammed the door.
She threw her backpack on the floor and took out her bunny.
She hugged it and said, "Don't worry, bunny.
We will go outside soon.
We will jump and make noises and have fun.

The bunny started to jump and make noises.
It was very loud and annoying.
Lily thought it was funny and laughed.
She jumped on the bed with the bunny and made noises too.
She did not care about the rain or her mom or anything else.
She only cared about her bunny and herself.
She was very selfish.
<|endoftext|> Lily and Ben were playing in the park.
They saw a big stick on the ground.
Lily wanted to use the stick as a sword.
Ben wanted to use the stick as a wand.
"Give me the stick, Lily.
I want to be a wizard," Ben said.
"No, Ben.
I want to be a knight.
The stick is my sword," Lily said.
They both pulled the stick and tried to take it from each other.
The stick broke in half.
Lily and Ben were sad and angry.
A lady was walking by with her dog.
She saw Lily and Ben and their broken stick.
She smiled and said, "Hello, children.
Do you know what you can do with your stick?" Lily and Ben shook their heads.
They did not know.
The lady said, "You can use your stick to make something beautiful.
You can use your stick to draw on the sand, or to make a picture with leaves and flowers, or to build a house for your toys.
You can use your stick to create and share, not to fight and break." She gave them each a half of the stick and said, "Here, you can have one piece each.
Now you have two sticks, and you can both play with them.
But remember, sticks are not for hurting, they are for helping." Lily and Ben looked at their sticks and then at each other.
They felt sorry for what they did.
They said, "Thank you, lady.
You are very kind.
We are sorry we fought over the stick.
We will use our sticks to make something beautiful." They hugged and said, "We are friends again." The lady and her dog smiled and walked away.
Lily and Ben used their sticks to draw a big heart on the sand.
They wrote their names inside the heart.
They were happy and proud of their beautiful stick art.
They learned that sharing is better than fighting, and that sticks can be used for good, not for bad.

<|endoftext|> Ben and Mia liked to play with their toys in the garden.
They had many toys, but their favorite was a big red car with four wheels and a horn.
They took turns to drive the car and make loud noises.
One day, they found a shiny button on the grass.
It was round and silver and had four holes.
They wondered what it was for.
"Maybe it is a magic button," Ben said.
"Maybe it can make things happen." "Like what?" Mia asked.
"Like making the car go faster, or making the flowers grow bigger, or making the sun shine brighter," Ben said.
They decided to try the button.
They put it on the car's dashboard and pressed it.
Nothing happened.
"Maybe we need to say a magic word," Mia said.
"Like what?" Ben said.
"Like abracadabra, or hocus pocus, or please," Mia said.
They tried different words, but nothing happened.
They were disappointed.
"Maybe it is not a magic button," Ben said.
"Maybe it is just a button." "Maybe it belongs to someone," Mia said.
"Maybe we should give it back." They agreed to look for the owner of the button.
They left the car and the button on the grass and went to ask their mom.
They did not know that the button was not just a button.
It was a remote control for a sprinkler system.
When they pressed it, they activated the sprinklers, but they did not see them because they were hidden behind the bushes.
The sprinklers started to spray water all over the garden, including the car and the button.
When Ben and Mia came back, they saw their car and their button soaked with water.
They were shocked and sad.
"Our car is wet!" Ben cried.
"Our button is wet!" Mia cried.
They ran to their car and tried to dry it with their hands and their clothes.
They also tried to dry the button, but it was too late.
The button was broken and did not work anymore.
They learned a lesson that day.
They learned that some things are not what they seem, and that they should be careful with what they find.
They also learned that water can ruin things that are dry.
They decided to never play with buttons again.

<|endoftext|> Tom and Jen were two fish who liked to swim in the big sea.

<|endoftext|> Anna and Ben were playing in the park.
They liked to dig in the sand and look for shiny things.
Sometimes they found coins, buttons, or shells.
They put them in their pockets and showed them to their mom.
One day, they found something different.
It was a big, round, white thing.
It was not shiny, but it was smooth and heavy.
Anna picked it up and said, "Look, Ben, what is this?" Ben looked at it and said, "I don't know.
Maybe it is a mineral.
A mineral is a thing that comes from the ground.
Some minerals are hard, like rocks.
Some minerals are soft, like salt." Anna felt the white thing with her fingers.
It was not hard, but it was not soft either.
It was somewhere in between.
She said, "Let's examine it.
Maybe we can find out more about it." They examined the white thing.
They rolled it, tapped it, and smelled it.
They did not see any colors, patterns, or holes on it.
They did not hear any sounds, or smell any smells from it.
It was just a big, round, white thing.
They decided to take it home and show it to their mom.
Maybe she would know what it was.
They put it in their backpack and walked to their house.
When they got home, they ran to their mom and said, "Mom, mom, look what we found in the park!
It is a mineral, but we don't know what kind of mineral.
Can you tell us?" Their mom looked at the white thing and smiled.
She said, "Oh, you found a pearl.
A pearl is a very special kind of mineral.
It is made by a sea animal called an oyster.
An oyster lives in a shell, and sometimes a small thing gets inside the shell and bothers the oyster.
The oyster covers the small thing with many layers of a shiny, smooth, white material.
That material is called nacre.
After a long time, the small thing becomes a pearl." Anna and Ben were amazed.
They said, "Wow, a pearl!
That is so cool!
How did it get in the park?" Their mom said, "Maybe someone lost it, or maybe a bird dropped it.
Pearls are very valuable, because they are rare and beautiful.
You are very lucky to find one.
But you know what is more valuable than a pearl?" Anna and Ben shook their heads.
They said, "No, what is more valuable than a pearl?" Their mom said, "You are.
You are my precious pearls.
You are rare and beautiful, and I love you very much.
You make me happy every day.
Thank you for sharing your discovery with me." Anna and Ben hugged their mom and said, "We love you too, mom.
You are the best mom in the world.
Thank you for teaching us about pearls." The moral of the story is: Some things are more valuable than others, but nothing is more valuable than love and family.
